Cross-multiply and solve the quadratic equation for $p$:
$$(-2p)^2 = (2p + 6)(p + 2) \implies 4p^2 = 2p^2 + 10p + 12 \implies 2p^2 - 10p - 12 = 0$$
$$p^2 - 5p - 6 = 0 \implies (p - 6)(p + 1) = 0 \implies p = 6 \quad (\text{since } p > 0)$$

Calculate the first term $a$ and common ratio $r$ when $p = 6$:
$$a = 2(6) + 6 = 18$$
$$r = \frac{-2(6)}{18} = -\frac{12}{18} = -\frac{2}{3}$$

Calculate the sum to infinity using $S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - r}$:
$$S_\infty = \frac{18}{1 - \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)} = \frac{18}{\frac{5}{3}} = 18 \times \frac{3}{5} = \frac{54}{5} = 10.8$$
